what: The recurring-task projection of shared/expandTaskOccurrences.ts, as a table: which occurrences a recurring scheduled task shows inside a window (the real task on its own day, read-only projections on every other), one step of the same walk (nextTaskOccurrence), and what “move to this day” can be on a source that owns the date (occurrenceMoveTarget). Measured from the TypeScript before the port.
why: The calendar views on both surfaces and the widget snapshot expand the same series; a frontend that is not JavaScript has to expand it too, and the projected days must match the instances the backend spawner creates. The core answers POSITIONS and DAYS (which input task, which day, real or projected); the shell builds the copies and their ids.
writtenBy: src/intl/expandTaskOccurrences.measure.test.ts — a one-off, run once and deleted; its cases mirror src/intl/expandTaskOccurrences.test.ts plus the rows the port needs that those never had (a base after the window, an empty window, the default cap, the step cap, interval 0, a count end, invalid fixed dates, monthly without a day of month, a base off its listed weekday, two series in one list, in_progress).

whereItLives.note: Inside cal-core, like the other task fixtures: twelve adapter repositories compile cal-core, and an include_str! reaching out of the crate would break the day it moves.

notInThisTable.makeOccurrenceId_isRecurringProjection_r: the id encoding of a projection (`<id> occ <day>`) is the shell’s: the core answers which input task and which day, the shell builds the copy and its id, and decodes it back
notInThisTable.projectionOf: the copying of a task’s fields onto a projection (time of day rides along) — the shell’s
notInThisTable.fromBackend_toBackend: the form value ↔ wire conversion; the core reads the wire shape (`cal_core::TaskRecurrence`) directly, so the rules in this table are wire rules
notInThisTable.spawner: cal_core::spawn advances a completed task to its next instance with the same stepping; two rows here name where the projector answers differently (invalid fixed dates) — the projector’s answers are pinned, the spawner is not this table’s subject

shape.expand: {tasks, from, to, maxPerTask?} → [{task: index into tasks, day: YYYY-MM-DD or null, projection: bool}] in emission order: for each expandable task its occurrences in the window (the base day is the real task), non-expandable tasks pass through in place with their own day.
shape.next: {scheduled, rule (wire shape) | null} → the next occurrence key or null.
shape.wasTypeScript: a row marked wasTypeScript pins a JS artifact the port may decide against; it must then change the row on purpose, with a note.
shape.baseTask: the Task every case’s task entries are overrides over

expand.name: daily-projects-every-day-in-the-window
expand.note: Both window ends inclusive; the time of day rides each occurrence (the shell copies it).

expand.name: the-real-task-is-the-one-on-its-own-day
expand.note: The occurrence on the task’s own scheduled_date is the real, interactive task; every other one is a projection.

expand.name: honours-the-interval
expand.note: Every 2 days.

expand.name: weekly-by-day-projects-only-the-listed-weekdays
expand.note: 2026-05-04 is a Monday; Mon/Wed/Fri.

expand.name: weekly-plain-steps-seven-days
expand.note: No listed weekdays: seven days per step, times the interval.

expand.name: base-not-on-a-listed-weekday-still-emits-itself
expand.note: 2026-05-05 is a Tuesday and the rule says Monday: the base day is the real task anyway; the walk continues on the next Monday.

expand.name: monthly-day-of-month-clamps-to-short-months
expand.note: Jan 31 → Feb 28 → Mar 31 → Apr 30: the day of month is re-applied every step.

expand.name: monthly-without-day-of-month-steps-from-the-clamped-date
expand.note: Without a day of month the step starts from the date reached: Jan 31 → Feb 28 → Mar 28, not back to the 31st.

expand.name: yearly-clamps-feb-29
expand.note: A Feb-29 anchor lands on Feb 28 in non-leap years.

expand.name: yearly-interval-two
expand.note: Every second year.

expand.name: fixed-dates-drive-a-seasonal-schedule
expand.note: April 1 and October 1, every year; the frequency is ignored.

expand.name: fixed-dates-clamp-the-day-to-the-month
expand.note: Feb 30 is Feb 28 (or 29).

expand.name: a-fixed-date-with-day-32-is-dropped
expand.note: The wire can carry day 32 or month 13; the TypeScript drops such a trigger (sanitize) instead of clamping it. With no trigger left, the frequency walks. The backend spawner clamps the day instead — a difference between spawner and projector, pinned as the projector answers today.

expand.name: fixed-dates-with-an-until-bound
expand.note: The bound applies to fixed triggers as well.

expand.name: stops-at-the-until-bound
expand.note: The bound day itself still emits; the day after does not.

expand.name: an-until-before-the-base-emits-nothing
expand.note: Already ended at the first step: not even the base day.

expand.name: a-count-end-is-not-an-end-here
expand.note: The projector only honours a date bound; an occurrence count is the provider’s (the spawner does the same). Pinned as it is.

expand.name: base-before-the-window-gives-only-projections
expand.note: None of the emitted days is the base day.

expand.name: a-base-after-the-window-emits-nothing
expand.note: The walk only goes forward: a series that starts after the window is absent from it — not passed through.

expand.name: far-past-daily-base-reaches-the-window
expand.note: The cap counts emissions, not the walk: an old, never-completed daily task keeps its original date and must still arrive in the window.

expand.name: far-past-weekly-by-day-base-reaches-the-window
expand.note: 2025-01-06 is a Monday; Mon/Thu. 2026-07-06 is a Monday, 07-09 a Thursday.

expand.name: interval-with-named-weekdays-is-not-dropped
expand.note: “Every 2 weeks on Monday” is every second Monday, not every Monday. 2026-08-03 is a Monday.

expand.name: every-listed-day-of-the-weeks-the-interval-lands-on
expand.note: Mon+Thu every two weeks is both days of every second week.

expand.name: an-until-before-the-window-emits-nothing-and-terminates
expand.note: A far-past bounded series stops at its bound instead of walking to the window.

expand.name: caps-at-max-per-task
expand.note: The first five emissions, then stop.

expand.name: max-per-task-zero-emits-nothing
expand.note: A zero budget emits nothing at all.

expand.name: the-default-cap-is-400
expand.note: Two years of a daily rule render 400 occurrences.

expand.name: a-base-beyond-the-step-cap-emits-nothing
expand.note: The walk is bounded by 100 000 steps (≈ 270 daily years); a base further back than that never reaches the window. Termination over completeness.

expand.name: interval-zero-on-a-scheduled-rule-counts-as-one
expand.note: The wire can carry interval 0 (a backlog rule’s “immediately”); a scheduled walk treats it as 1.

expand.name: an-empty-window-emits-nothing-and-passes-the-rest-through
expand.note: from after to: the recurring task is absent, the plain one passes through as always.

expand.name: non-recurring-passes-through
expand.note: Verbatim, whatever its date.

expand.name: an-undated-plain-task-passes-through
expand.note: Pass-through keeps a null day.

expand.name: from-completion-passes-through
expand.note: Its future dates depend on when each turn is checked off: unknowable ahead of time.

expand.name: backlog-placement-passes-through
expand.note: Its next turn is undated.

expand.name: no-scheduled-date-passes-through
expand.note: A deadline is not a base.

expand.name: completed-passes-through
expand.note: A terminal instance never projects: its future days belong to the next open instance the backend spawns.

expand.name: cancelled-passes-through
expand.note: Terminal as well.

expand.name: in-progress-expands
expand.note: Only completed and cancelled are terminal.

expand.name: mixed-list-keeps-input-order
expand.note: A task’s occurrences stay together, tasks stay in input order.

expand.name: two-series-in-input-order
expand.note: The second series follows the first, not interleaved by day.

expand.name: an-empty-scheduled-date-vanishes
expand.note: A JS artifact: "" is not null, parses to an invalid date, and the walk ends with nothing emitted — the task is absent. No producer writes "" (API rows carry null); a port is free to read "" as undated and pass the task through, and must then change this row on purpose.

next.name: weekly-by-day-is-the-next-listed-day
next.note: 2026-06-25 is a Thursday; Mon/Fri → Friday the 26th.

next.name: weekly-by-day-jumps-the-interval-when-the-week-is-spent
next.note: Thursday, rule Monday every 2 weeks → the Monday of the week after next.

next.name: monthly-from-a-clamped-day-stays-there
next.note: Feb 28 → Mar 28 without a day of month.

next.name: fixed-dates-wrap-to-next-year
next.note: After October 1, the next trigger is April 1 of next year.

next.name: all-invalid-fixed-dates-fall-back-to-the-frequency
next.note: The TypeScript drops invalid triggers before it looks, so none are left and the frequency walks. The spawner keeps them and finds no trigger. Pinned as the projector answers.

next.name: past-an-until-end-is-null
next.note: The next step is after the bound.

next.name: on-the-until-day-is-kept
next.note: The bound day itself is a valid step.

next.name: a-count-end-does-not-end
next.note: Only a date bound ends the walk here.

move.name: advances-the-series-where-the-source-owns-the-date
move.note: iOS Reminders: the due date is the series anchor; one step forward is what it can do, and the caller is told.

move.name: does-not-invent-a-day-when-clearing
move.note: Clearing is clearing on every source.

move.name: an-ended-series-keeps-the-requested-day
move.note: No later turn: failing to move is better than moving somewhere invented.

move.name: a-backlog-rule-still-advances-by-its-step
move.note: The move does not ask about placement or anchor; only the projector does.
